pathway.title: CVS HEALTH Corp — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: First, leverage and cover have improved on both numerator and denominator. Total debt carrying value fell from USD 64,570 million at December 31, 2025 to USD 60,680 million at September 30, 2026 while LTM adjusted EBITDA rose from USD 17,073 million to USD 19,837 million, taking total debt to adjusted EBITDA from 3.78x to 3.06x and net debt to adjusted EBITDA from 3.29x to 2.47x [CP-1]. The mechanic is repayment of USD 4,057 million of long-term debt with no issuance in nine months 2026 and higher earnings, so debt service is better covered. The implication is lower refinancing and leverage risk, but the EBITDA is our construct because the company reports none and discloses no covenant definition.

Second, the earnings recovery is concentrated. Adjusted operating income by segment moved from USD 14,443 million at FY2025 to USD 17,098 million on LTM Q3 2026; Health Care Benefits rose by USD 2,764 million while Health Services rose by USD 100 million, Pharmacy & Consumer Wellness by USD 178 million and Corporate/Other fell by USD 387 million (Calculations). Health Care Benefits recorded an implied loss of USD 676 million in Q4 2025 [CP-1], so the LTM window replaces a weak quarter, and its medical benefit ratio of 87.8 percent for nine months 2026 against 90.0 percent reflects the absence of 2025 premium deficiency reserves and lower favorable prior period development [CP-1A]. The mechanic is underwriting leverage on a large premium base; the implication is that a reversal would raise leverage quickly (see the sensitivity below).

Third, liquidity is adequate but less deep than the consolidated cash suggests. Consolidated cash of USD 11,738 million includes about USD 5,900 million held by the parent or nonrestricted subsidiaries, plus USD 7,500 million of undrawn facilities that now expire in May 2029, 2030 and 2031, and no commercial paper [CP-1]. Against that, the next twelve months include a current portion of long-term debt of USD 3,457 million, a dividend of about USD 3,423 million on an LTM basis and an opioid settlement obligation whose current portion was USD 648 million at December 31, 2025, together USD 7,528 million; parent-level liquidity of USD 13,400 million covers that 1.78x. The weak spots are that letters of credit on the facilities are not supplied and that nine months 2026 operating cash flow of USD 15,318 million was helped by working-capital timing.

Fourth, claims outside the debt figure and a structural change sit over the credit. The opioid accrual was about USD 3.4 billion at September 30, 2026, operating lease liabilities were USD 14,617 million, the Omnicare guarantee charge was USD 193 million, and the separation announced on November 4, 2026 would create two companies [CP-1, CP-1A]. The mechanic is competing calls on cash and a possible change of obligor or guarantors; the implication is that leverage on the debt figure alone understates claims, and the amendment, assumption or guarantee route for the notes is the main monitoring item.

Fifth, the information that would let a committee set protections is missing. Covenant levels and headroom, issuer and guarantor by series, indenture terms and letters of credit are not supplied, and ownership detail is not in the pack [CP-0, CP-1, CP-1A]. The ratings (BBB at Fitch with a Negative outlook, Baa3 at Moody's with a Positive outlook, BBB at S&P with a Stable outlook, company statements) are described by the company as investment grade, and one agency holds a Negative outlook. The implication is that the view is a fundamental one and the protection analysis is unfinished.

runs.text: Strengths. The group has scale and diversification across insurance, pharmacy benefits and retail pharmacy, with USD 420,614 million of LTM revenue and adjusted operating income positive in three of four segments [CP-1]. Deleveraging has been funded from internal cash flow, with USD 12,144 million of LTM free cash flow after dividends, no 2026 issuance and no share repurchases in nine months 2026 [CP-1, CP-1A]. Liquidity is supported by USD 7,500 million of undrawn facilities with the earliest expiry in May 2029, so no facility matures within twelve months [CP-1]. The maturity profile is manageable in the near term, with USD 3,379 million due in 2027 and USD 5,008 million in 2028 per the schedule at December 31, 2025, against LTM free cash flow of USD 15,567 million and the facilities [CP-1]. Reporting is regular and discloses segment reconciliations and subsequent events [CP-1A].

Weaknesses. Earnings are concentrated: Health Care Benefits drove the improvement and about 20 percent of consolidated revenue comes from the federal government, mainly Medicare contracts [CP-1A]. Protections cannot be assessed because covenant levels, guarantors and indentures are not supplied [CP-0, CP-1]. Cash is partly outside the parent, and letters of credit usage is unknown [CP-1]. The debt stack includes USD 3,000 million of junior subordinated notes in two series and unsecured senior notes, so structural and ranking questions arise on a separation [CP-1]. Claims outside debt are large: the opioid accrual, lease liabilities and the Omnicare guarantee [CP-1, CP-1A]. The separation introduces an unresolved change of obligor, and pharmacy segments face reimbursement and price pressure, with Pharmacy & Consumer Wellness revenue down 2.0 percent in Q3 2026 [CP-1A].

runs.text: The only announced transaction is a proposed separation of CVS Health into two independent, publicly traded companies, announced on November 4, 2026 and disclosed as a subsequent event to the September 30, 2026 financial statements (Q3 10-Q page:40 and page:44). It is intended to be tax-free to the Company and its shareholders for U.S. federal income tax purposes. One company would hold Aetna, CVS Caremark, CVS Specialty, Oak Street Health and Signify Health and would carry the CVS Health name in the interim; the other would hold retail pharmacy, mail pharmacy, MinuteClinic including virtual care and the Health100 technology services business and would be named CVS Pharmacy. Completion is expected in the first half of 2028, subject to customary conditions including final approval by the Board, effectiveness of a Form 10 registration statement and a customary confirmation of tax-free treatment. This is a labelled future date, not a fact. The pack gives no purchase price, use of proceeds, new debt, debt allocation, guarantee, change-of-control or covenant treatment for the separation, so its liquidity and leverage effect is Insufficient Information. The creditor mechanic is that two entities will replace one obligor and the existing indentures and facilities will have to be dealt with; whether that is by assumption, guarantee, exchange or retained parent obligations is unknown, and that is the main monitoring item.

On new debt issues, no debt was issued in nine months 2026 (the cash flow statement shows no proceeds from long-term debt and repayments of long-term debt, Q3 10-Q page:4). Earlier issuance in the notes: on May 9, 2024 senior notes of about 5.0 billion dollars in five series for general corporate purposes; on December 10, 2024 two junior subordinated series of 2.25 billion and 750 million dollars with fixed-to-fixed rate resets, whose proceeds funded a cash tender in which about 2.6 billion dollars of senior notes were bought for about 2.0 billion dollars in cash with a gain on early extinguishment of 491 million dollars; and on August 15, 2025 senior notes in four series of 750 million, 1.5 billion, 1.25 billion and 500 million dollars due 2032, 2035, 2055 and 2065 with total proceeds of about 4.0 billion dollars used to repay existing indebtedness including commercial paper and for general corporate purposes (10-K page:151 to page:152). The creditor reading is that the Company has used long-dated issuance and a liability management tender to extend and reshape the stack, and has since moved to repayment. Other transactions relevant to credit are the Omnicare matters and the Rite Aid asset acquisitions below.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The financial base is usable and shows improving credit metrics, with limits that the committee should hold alongside the ratios. On adjusted EBITDA built as adjusted operating income plus depreciation and amortization less amortization of intangibles, total debt to EBITDA is 3.78x at FY2025 and 3.06x on LTM Q3 2026, net debt to EBITDA 3.29x and 2.47x, and EBITDA to cash interest 5.71x and 6.51x. Both parts of the leverage move contributed: total debt carrying value fell from 64,570 to 60,680 while LTM adjusted EBITDA rose from 17,073 to 19,837. The LTM window now excludes the large 2025 add-backs, so reported and adjusted EBITDA are close on LTM Q3 2026 (19,581 against 19,837), whereas at FY2025 they differ by 7,807, mainly a non-cash goodwill impairment of 5,725. The company reports no EBITDA and the filings disclose no covenant definition or level, so every ratio here is an analyst construct and headroom is Not calculable. Cash is flattered as a deleveraging input: consolidated cash of 11,738 includes cash held outside the parent, and net debt on the parent and nonrestricted cash of about 5,900 gives 2.76x rather than 2.47x. Cash flow from operations for nine months 2026 was 15,318 against 7,249 a year earlier, with the Q3 10-Q attributing the increase to timing of receipts and payments and improved Health Care Benefits performance, so the LTM free cash flow of 15,567 is not a steady-state run rate. Claims outside the debt figure include an opioid settlement accrual of about 3,400, operating lease liabilities of 14,617, the Omnicare guarantee charge of 193 and an announced separation whose financing terms are not supplied.

fields.value: Method: each material conclusion runs from a located quote or figure to a risk mechanic to a credit implication. Facts are tagged Documentary Fact, Management Language, Analyst Interpretation or Insufficient Information. Figures that also appear in the financial base handoff are used exactly as stated there. The upstream handoffs are used as supplied; the one correction carried from the financial base handoff (47 of the 49 note lines carry a balance at December 31, 2025) is repeated where it matters. fields.name: Quote
fields.value: CVS Health is a diversified, listed health care company with four reportable segments: Health Care Benefits (the Aetna insurer), Health Services (the CVS Caremark pharmacy benefit manager plus clinical and care delivery businesses including Signify Health and Oak Street Health), Pharmacy & Consumer Wellness (the retail and infusion pharmacy business) and Corporate/Other. For a creditor the mechanics are: a very large, low-margin revenue base dominated by drug pass-through; an insurance segment whose results swing on the medical benefit ratio and on government rate and risk-adjustment policy; a pharmacy segment under reimbursement and price pressure; and a group that carries a large debt stack with unsecured senior notes and two junior subordinated series. The recent history that matters is a reset in 2025 (a goodwill impairment in the care delivery business, exits from accountable care programs, an individual exchange premium deficiency and the Omnicare bankruptcy) followed by a stronger 2026 in which Health Care Benefits recovered and the group repaid debt while leaving the dividend unchanged. The leading uncertainty is the announced separation: it is a proposed transaction, not a completed one, and nothing in the pack says how existing notes, facilities, guarantees or the junior subordinated notes would be allocated. There is no sponsor, no leveraged buyout and no sponsor behaviour to assess, so the governance review rests on documented issuer actions only, and ownership and control detail is Insufficient Information because the proxy statement is incorporated by reference and not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The only announced transaction is a proposed separation of CVS Health into two independent, publicly traded companies, announced on November 4, 2026 and disclosed as a subsequent event to the September 30, 2026 financial statements (Q3 10-Q page:40 and page:44). It is intended to be tax-free to the Company and its shareholders for U.S. federal income tax purposes. One company would hold Aetna, CVS Caremark, CVS Specialty, Oak Street Health and Signify Health and would carry the CVS Health name in the interim; the other would hold retail pharmacy, mail pharmacy, MinuteClinic including virtual care and the Health100 technology services business and would be named CVS Pharmacy. Completion is expected in the first half of 2028, subject to customary conditions including final approval by the Board, effectiveness of a Form 10 registration statement and a customary confirmation of tax-free treatment. This is a labelled future date, not a fact. The pack gives no purchase price, use of proceeds, new debt, debt allocation, guarantee, change-of-control or covenant treatment for the separation, so its liquidity and leverage effect is Insufficient Information. Implication: revenue durability is good but margin resilience depends on government rates and medical cost trend, so leverage tolerance should be tested for a reversal in the Government business medical benefit ratio. fields.value: 2. Margin and cash flow risk. Evidence: the medical benefit ratio was 87.8 percent for nine months 2026 against 90.0 percent, with lower favorable prior period development (Q3 10-Q page:55), and Health Care Benefits adjusted operating income rose strongly (financial base handoff). Mechanic: small changes in the ratio on a premium base of this size move group earnings. Implication: the improvement in leverage reported in the financial base handoff rests on one segment and is not yet a through-the-cycle measure; monitoring should centre on medical cost trend and prior period development.

Mechanic: PBM contracts reprice at renewal and legislation targets PBM activities (Q3 10-Q page:48). Implication: the largest client terms are not disclosed, so concentration inside the PBM cannot be judged.

Mechanic: each is a claim or a structural change that the debt figure does not capture. fields.value: Fundamental credit synthesis for CVS HEALTH Corp (issuer id cvs, registrant CVS Health Corporation), as of 2026-11-05, pathway credit_snapshot. It combines the financial base [CP-1] and the business and transaction context [CP-1A] into a credit view, key findings, strengths, weaknesses and risks, in USD with Q3 2026 as the current period and FY2025 as the prior period. It gives no peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The figures are taken from the two upstream handoffs; the source files were reopened only to confirm the figures used below (the debt table, liquidity, ratings, segment tables and the separation note) and to search again for covenant terms, letters of credit and guarantor detail.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: CVS Health Corporation is an improving, moderate-leverage credit whose 2026 progress rests heavily on one segment. The strongest support is deleveraging: total debt to adjusted EBITDA fell to 3.06x on LTM Q3 2026 from 3.78x at FY2025, adjusted EBITDA to cash interest rose to 6.51x, and undrawn back-up facilities of USD 7,500 million sit beside cash of USD 11,738 million. The weakest point is that Health Care Benefits supplied more than the whole net rise in adjusted operating income, while covenant levels, guarantor terms and the debt allocation under the announced separation are not disclosed. What decides the outcome is whether the medical benefit ratio holds, and what the separation does to the obligor and guarantee structure before completion, expected in the first half of 2028.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: First, leverage and cover have improved on both numerator and denominator. Total debt carrying value fell from USD 64,570 million at December 31, 2025 to USD 60,680 million at September 30, 2026 while LTM adjusted EBITDA rose from USD 17,073 million to USD 19,837 million, taking total debt to adjusted EBITDA from 3.78x to 3.06x and net debt to adjusted EBITDA from 3.29x to 2.47x [CP-1]. The mechanic is repayment of USD 4,057 million of long-term debt with no issuance in nine months 2026 and higher earnings, so debt service is better covered. The implication is lower refinancing and leverage risk, but the EBITDA is our construct because the company reports none and discloses no covenant definition.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Second, the earnings recovery is concentrated. Adjusted operating income by segment moved from USD 14,443 million at FY2025 to USD 17,098 million on LTM Q3 2026; Health Care Benefits rose by USD 2,764 million while Health Services rose by USD 100 million, Pharmacy & Consumer Wellness by USD 178 million and Corporate/Other fell by USD 387 million (Calculations). Health Care Benefits recorded an implied loss of USD 676 million in Q4 2025 [CP-1], so the LTM window replaces a weak quarter, and its medical benefit ratio of 87.8 percent for nine months 2026 against 90.0 percent reflects the absence of 2025 premium deficiency reserves and lower favorable prior period development [CP-1A]. The mechanic is underwriting leverage on a large premium base; the implication is that a reversal would raise leverage quickly (see the sensitivity below).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Third, liquidity is adequate but less deep than the consolidated cash suggests. Consolidated cash of USD 11,738 million includes about USD 5,900 million held by the parent or nonrestricted subsidiaries, plus USD 7,500 million of undrawn facilities that now expire in May 2029, 2030 and 2031, and no commercial paper [CP-1]. Against that, the next twelve months include a current portion of long-term debt of USD 3,457 million, a dividend of about USD 3,423 million on an LTM basis and an opioid settlement obligation whose current portion was USD 648 million at December 31, 2025, together USD 7,528 million; parent-level liquidity of USD 13,400 million covers that 1.78x. The weak spots are that letters of credit on the facilities are not supplied and that nine months 2026 operating cash flow of USD 15,318 million was helped by working-capital timing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fourth, claims outside the debt figure and a structural change sit over the credit. The opioid accrual was about USD 3.4 billion at September 30, 2026, operating lease liabilities were USD 14,617 million, the Omnicare guarantee charge was USD 193 million, and the separation announced on November 4, 2026 would create two companies [CP-1, CP-1A]. The mechanic is competing calls on cash and a possible change of obligor or guarantors; the implication is that leverage on the debt figure alone understates claims, and the amendment, assumption or guarantee route for the notes is the main monitoring item.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fifth, the information that would let a committee set protections is missing. Covenant levels and headroom, issuer and guarantor by series, indenture terms and letters of credit are not supplied, and ownership detail is not in the pack [CP-0, CP-1, CP-1A]. The ratings (BBB at Fitch with a Negative outlook, Baa3 at Moody's with a Positive outlook, BBB at S&P with a Stable outlook, company statements) are described by the company as investment grade, and one agency holds a Negative outlook. The implication is that the view is a fundamental one and the protection analysis is unfinished.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. The group has scale and diversification across insurance, pharmacy benefits and retail pharmacy, with USD 420,614 million of LTM revenue and adjusted operating income positive in three of four segments [CP-1]. Deleveraging has been funded from internal cash flow, with USD 12,144 million of LTM free cash flow after dividends, no 2026 issuance and no share repurchases in nine months 2026 [CP-1, CP-1A]. Liquidity is supported by USD 7,500 million of undrawn facilities with the earliest expiry in May 2029, so no facility matures within twelve months [CP-1]. The maturity profile is manageable in the near term, with USD 3,379 million due in 2027 and USD 5,008 million in 2028 per the schedule at December 31, 2025, against LTM free cash flow of USD 15,567 million and the facilities [CP-1]. Reporting is regular and discloses segment reconciliations and subsequent events [CP-1A].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. Earnings are concentrated: Health Care Benefits drove the improvement and about 20 percent of consolidated revenue comes from the federal government, mainly Medicare contracts [CP-1A]. Protections cannot be assessed because covenant levels, guarantors and indentures are not supplied [CP-0, CP-1]. Cash is partly outside the parent, and letters of credit usage is unknown [CP-1]. The debt stack includes USD 3,000 million of junior subordinated notes in two series and unsecured senior notes, so structural and ranking questions arise on a separation [CP-1]. Claims outside debt are large: the opioid accrual, lease liabilities and the Omnicare guarantee [CP-1, CP-1A]. The separation introduces an unresolved change of obligor, and pharmacy segments face reimbursement and price pressure, with Pharmacy & Consumer Wellness revenue down 2.0 percent in Q3 2026 [CP-1A].
